public_rationale: This is a judgment about scientific explanation. Marcus says a good theory of language should explain why human language is as it is, and that GPT-3 does not. That standard is normative and has no stated measure. 'Merely mimic statistical patterns' describes what the model learned, and researchers disputed it. GPT-3 is trained to predict text (e1). Studies show such models both generalize and sometimes copy (e2). Neither finding settles whether GPT-3 offers 'remarkably little' explanation. No test can score this as true or false.
limitations: Context evidence covers GPT-2 and GPT-3 in general. It does not address 'explanation' directly.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Systems like GPT-3 offer very little explanation and only mimic statistical patterns of how language is used in their training data.

statement.excerpt: As it happens, systems like GPT-3 provide remarkably little in the way of explanation. They don’t tell us why the world is as it is; they merely mimic statistical patterns of how language has been used in their immense databases.

from_speaker: provide remarkably little in the way of explanation
don't tell us why the world is as it is
merely mimic statistical patterns of how language has been used
our_interpretation: The claim is about the scientific explanatory value of GPT-3 as a theory of human language. 'Remarkably little explanation' is a judgment about what counts as a good scientific explanation, with no measure attached.
'Merely mimic statistical patterns' is a contested description of what the model has learned. Researchers did not agree on it in 2022, and no single test was accepted as settling it.
Because the claim mixes a normative standard (what a good theory must explain) with a contested description, it has no plain reading that evidence could settle.
criteria.support_condition: None that is decisive. Evidence would need an agreed test showing GPT-3 explains nothing about language or the world beyond surface statistics.
criteria.contradiction_condition: None that is decisive. Evidence would need an agreed test showing GPT-3 gives real scientific explanations of why human language has the character it does.
